title: P104: 22 swap-then-delete composites on #7630, conditional kappa 0.0036807241001
body:
**Conditional κ = 0.0036807241001** (exact crossing 0.00368072410014727862067955898005, official bracket [0.0036807241001, 0.0036807241002]), **×1.00368972 over #7633** (κ ≥ 0.003667193194322). The base word is our #7630.

**The edits.** 22 composites on 44 helpers (`data/edits.json`, base-word coordinates). Each is a SWAP-NULL relabel of two helpers that are both born at {0} and end at V (the hubs undo it exactly; the swap law from our Lean package #7634), followed by deleting the stay at the swap chart that the relabel makes redundant. In every composite the receiver arrives blank, so after the relabel the co-resident register carries its own content along the receiver's old tail, the copy `b += a` becomes a rename, and the receiver's stop disappears. Plain deletion of the same stops fails.

Every ADD/SCALE at the {0} chart and at V is then re-derived jointly and exactly, so all 1,569 rows and end charts equal #7630's. The owned INIT/CLEAR/MOVE sequence is #7630's. S is 1,424, paid positions go from 110,026 to 109,652, and the word has 202,668 events. The ordinary bill is 859,783,396 (from #7630's 867,014,040), below 10^9.

**Premises: conditional on the same framework assumptions as #7630** (#7620's five assumptions and its 17·68 banks, over the same 180 CLEARs). 151 CLEAR contents change with the re-derived hub content, so all 180 CLEARs carry exact certificates under #7620's `verify_certificates` rule.

**Packaging.** The affected-pair census grows from 981 to 1,023 pairs (+42, none dropped), with the 512 + 512 column tests on all of them. `VERIFY.json` also runs the core replay, the 180 certificates with rejecting controls, the controls (14 rejecting, 2 accepting), and `price.py`; `research_package.py` passes end to end. Hashes, census, invoice and bracket are pinned.

**Credit.** Our #7630, #7623 and #7621 for the base; SYLforge (#7616, #7620) for the device inside it; rohanarun's #7113 caller. DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code.
